title: LMDB-backed storage layer
description: Replace src/cask.rs with an LMDB-backed storage layer. Phase 1: schemaless tables with surrogate u64 keys, end-to-end via heed. Phase 2: typed composite PKs and SQLite-style Seek*/Idx* opcodes for prefix-range planning. Branching deferred (see storage-plan.md Appendix A). Reference docs: storage-plan.md, storage-reference.md.

title: Grammar + IR: schemaless tables with key-column lists
description:
Replace the current 'create table foo (Type)' grammar with 'create table foo (col Type, ...)' where each column declares a typed key. Tables are schemaless — only PK columns are declared.

Files to change:
- src/parser.lalrpop:91-93 — replace TableDefinition. Add KeyColumns and KeyColumn rules.
- src/lexer.rs — ensure 'int' and 'string' tokens exist (string already does, int may not).
- src/ir.rs — replace Table::schema: Type with Table::keys: Vec<KeyColumn>. Add KeyColumn { name, typ } and KeyType enum (Int, String). Update ir::table_definition action to take Option<Vec<KeyColumn>>.
- src/compiler.rs — cc_create currently inspects Table::schema; update to consume Table::keys (still ignored at storage level in P1 — no validation needed yet, that lands in Task 4).
- Existing tests using the old type-body syntax: rewrite to the new key-column syntax.

Acceptance:
- These all parse and round-trip through the IR:
    create table points;
    create table points (x int);
    create table points (x int, y int);
    create table users (id string);
- cargo test green.
- No storage-layer changes in this task.
acceptance_criteria: create table foo; create table foo (x int); create table foo (x int, y int); create table foo (id string) all parse, build the new IR, and existing tests pass.
close_reason: Grammar accepts the new key-column syntax; IR types updated; all four plan-mandated CREATE TABLE examples round-trip (parse → IR → Display → parse). 11/13 lib tests pass; the 2 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (Connection::memory() todo, parse_acceptance_fetch uses unsupported fetch keyword).

title: Storage module skeleton (P1): env + catalog + codecs + cursor + txn
description:
Build src/storage/ as a self-contained module. P1 surface: surrogate u64 keys only, no typed PK extraction yet.

New files:
- src/storage/mod.rs — MonaDB struct (heed::Env + Dbs handle), Row { oid, val }, public re-exports.
- src/storage/env.rs — heed env init (max_dbs=8, EnvFlags::NO_SUB_DIR for single-file layout, configurable map_size with a 1 GiB default).
- src/storage/catalog.rs — TableSchema, table_id allocation, schema CRUD on the meta DB. Layout per storage-plan.md §LMDB physical layout.
- src/storage/keycodec.rs — P1 only: surrogate u64_be(row_id). Counter at meta[b"row_seq/<u32_be(table_id)>"].
- src/storage/value_codec.rs — TAG_LIVE = 0x00 prefix byte + serde_json::to_vec round-trip.
- src/storage/cursor.rs — StorageCursor: prefix-walk over u32_be(table_id), strip leading tag byte, no range_end (per the plan update).
- src/storage/txn.rs — ReadTxn, WriteTxn with staged BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>>; flush on commit appending the 8-byte zero suffix.
- src/storage/error.rs — StorageError, From<heed::Error>, KeyTooLong.
- Cargo.toml: add heed = "0.20", byteorder = "1.5".

This task does NOT touch src/vm.rs, src/connection.rs, or src/cask.rs. The module is self-contained and unit-tested in isolation.

Tests: src/storage/cursor.rs and src/storage/txn.rs ship with module-level #[cfg(test)] tests against a temp dir — create table, put_row with surrogates, scan cursor, assert order, drop+reopen for durability.

Acceptance:
- cargo build green with the new module.
- Module-level tests cover: create_table, put_row with surrogate keys, full-table-scan cursor, multi-table prefix isolation, durability across reopen.
- No regression in existing tests (the module is unused by VM at this point).
acceptance_criteria: src/storage/ compiles and ships unit tests for surrogate-key put/scan + durability. VM and Connection are unchanged, so existing tests still pass.

title: VM + Connection wire-up; delete cask.rs and cursor.rs (Phase 1 e2e)
description:
Replace the cask-backed Connection/VM path with the MonaDB façade. After this task, the REPL is durably backed by LMDB end-to-end with surrogate keys.

Changes:
- src/connection.rs — rewrite as a thin adapter wrapping MonaDB. Connection holds Arc<heed::Env> via MonaDB; per-statement begin_read/begin_write. Keep public method names where possible to minimize churn.
- src/vm.rs:
  - Add txn: TxnHandle<'a> field on VM<'a>.
  - Vop::Init opens read or write txn based on a compile-time flag set by the compiler.
  - Vop::Open(table) calls self.txn.open_cursor(table).
  - Vop::Insert/InsertBatch call self.txn.put_row(...).
  - Vop::Commit finalizes the txn.
  - Vop::Rewind/Next/Load unchanged.
- src/compiler.rs — annotate the program prelude with read vs write txn flavor (any Insert/InsertBatch/CreateTable/Drop/Clear ⇒ write).
- Move Row from src/cursor.rs into src/storage/mod.rs. **Delete src/cursor.rs.**
- **Delete src/cask.rs.** Drop the 'bytes' dep from Cargo.toml if unused after.
- Update tests: connection tests use the old type-body syntax (already migrated in Task 1); make them target the LMDB path.

New tests:
- tests/storage_phase1.rs — open temp MonaDB, create tables (with and without PK syntax), insert rows, scan; reopen path, scan again, assert durability.
- tests/vm_e2e.rs — full RQL → VM → storage path: 'create table foo (x int); insert into foo ({x: 1}); select * from foo;'.

Acceptance:
- cargo test green; cargo run REPL: 'create table x; insert into x (1); insert into x (2); select * from x;' returns 2 rows.
- src/cask.rs and src/cursor.rs do not exist.
- Database is durable: REPL state survives process restart on the same path.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end LMDB-backed create+insert+select works in REPL. cask.rs and cursor.rs deleted. tests/storage_phase1.rs and tests/vm_e2e.rs pass. Durability across restart verified.

title: Phase 2 codec + typed PK extraction
description:
Add typed key codec and wire it through put_row.

Changes:
- src/storage/keycodec.rs:
  - encode_string(s): UTF-8 + 0x00→00 01 / 0x01→00 02 escape + 00 00 terminator.
  - encode_int(i): i64 sign-biased BE (XOR high bit).
  - encode_composite(values, schema): loop over Table::keys producing enc(c_1) || ... || enc(c_N).
  - encode_partial(values, schema): for partial-prefix seeks (values.len() < schema.len()) — emits prefix form, no trailing components. Used in Task 5 for Seek*/Idx* with ncols < pk_arity.
- src/compiler.rs — cc_create validation: at most one PK clause, column names unique, types are Int or String.
- src/storage/txn.rs — WriteTxn::put_row: extract PK column values from the row JSON by top-level field name, type-check against the schema, encode in declaration order. Tables with no keys continue using surrogates. Enforce LMDB key-length limit (≤511 bytes); surface KeyTooLong.

Tests:
- Unit tests for each codec function, including: byte-stuffing round-trip for strings, sign bias for negative ints, composite N=1/2/3 cases, encode_partial with values.len() < schema.len().
- put_row test: create table with typed PK, insert two rows, read back via full-table-scan cursor, verify byte order matches logical order.

Acceptance:
- create table events (tenant string, user string, ts int); + inserts + select * from events; returns rows in (tenant, user, ts) order.
- Negative ints sort before positive ints. String '0x00' bytes round-trip correctly.
- Partial-key encoding for prefix seeks is exercised in the encode_partial unit tests (the planner will use it in Task 6).
acceptance_criteria: Typed PK extraction works in put_row; codec unit tests cover round-trip and sort-order properties; rows insert via real PKs and scan in correct byte order.

title: Seek*/Idx* cursor methods + Vops + emit helpers
description:
Add the SQLite-style positioning and termination opcodes; this task is mechanical wire-up of the surface — the planner that uses it lands in Task 6.

Changes:
- src/storage/cursor.rs — add 8 methods on StorageCursor (signatures per storage-plan.md):
    seek_ge/gt/le/lt(&mut self, key: &[Value]) -> bool
    idx_ge/gt/le/lt(&self, key: &[Value]) -> bool
  Each encodes the partial tuple via keycodec::encode_partial (or encode_composite for full arity), then either positions the inner heed cursor or does a bytewise compare against the current key.
- src/vm.rs — add 8 Vop variants:
    SeekGE/GT/LE/LT(c: usize, ncols: usize, jmp: usize)
    IdxGE/GT/LE/LT(c: usize, ncols: usize, jmp: usize)
  Implement dispatch in next(): pop ncols values, hand to cursor as &[Value], jump on the documented condition. Mirror the existing Rewind/Next dispatch shape.
- src/compiler.rs — emit_seek_ge / emit_seek_gt / emit_seek_le / emit_seek_lt and emit_idx_ge / emit_idx_gt / emit_idx_le / emit_idx_lt helpers. patch() accepts the new opcodes (they have a jump target at offset 2).

Tests:
- src/storage/cursor.rs unit tests: against canned data (table_id=7 with composite PK), exercise:
    - seek_ge with full-arity tuple positioning to first match
    - seek_ge with partial-prefix tuple (ncols < pk_arity)
    - seek_ge returning false when no row matches
    - idx_ge / idx_gt comparisons against a current position with both partial and full tuples
- VM-level test in src/vm.rs: hand-built Vop program exercising SeekGE+IdxGT.

Acceptance:
- All 8 cursor methods implemented and unit-tested.
- All 8 Vops dispatch correctly via a hand-built program.
- No planner changes yet — cc_iter still emits Rewind/Next exclusively.
acceptance_criteria: Cursor methods + Vops compile and pass unit tests. VM dispatches the new opcodes correctly. Planner still emits Rewind/Next.

title: cc_iter planner with PkBounds + Phase 2 e2e tests
description:
Teach the compiler to recognize WHERE-clause prefixes against the leading PK columns and emit Seek*/Idx* instead of Rewind/Next.

Changes:
- src/compiler.rs:
  - Define PkBounds { equalities: Vec<Expr>, range: Option<(RangeOp, Expr)> } (or similar) and an analyzer fn analyze_pk_bounds(where_: &Option<Expr>, pk_schema: &[KeyColumn]) -> (PkBounds, Option<Expr> /* residual */).
  - Change cc_iter signature: take where_: &Option<Expr> as a new parameter; return IterPatches { loop_top: usize, exits: Vec<Patch> } instead of usize.
  - Compile shape:
      No PK bounds → Open + Rewind (Phase 1 path).
      Bounds present → Open + push lower-tuple + SeekGE/GT(ncols=k) + (loop_top) push upper-tuple + IdxGT/GE(ncols=k) + body + Next jumping to loop_top.
      Residual → keep IfNot inside loop after Idx*.
  - cc_select consumes IterPatches.exits via the existing to_patch list (compiler.rs:133–135 unchanged in shape).

Tests (new tests/storage_phase2.rs and compiler-level Vop assertions):
- 'create table events (tenant string, user string, ts int); ... select * from events where tenant = "acme";' compiles to Open+SeekGE(ncols=1)+IdxGT(ncols=1)+body+Next. Verify by inspecting the emitted Vop program.
- where x = 1 and y = 2 on (x int, y int) ⇒ ncols=2 on both sides.
- where ts >= 100 and ts < 200 (no leading-PK constraint) ⇒ falls back to Rewind+Next + residual IfNot.
- where x >= 1 and x < 5 and other_field = 'foo' ⇒ x range becomes Seek/Idx; other_field = 'foo' becomes residual IfNot.
- End-to-end query results match a brute-force full-table-scan baseline.

Acceptance:
- All four predicate-shape examples compile to the expected Vop sequences.
- Range queries return correct results.
- Phase 1 path (no PK bound) is byte-identical in emitted Vops to pre-Task-6.
acceptance_criteria: cc_iter analyzes WHERE for PK prefixes and emits Seek/Idx + residual IfNot. Phase 2 e2e tests pass. No regression on Phase 1 path.
